schema.title: short screen title
schema.summary: 1-2 line purpose of the module or menu

items.key: exact menu key the user types (or service name when there is no menu)
items.title: menu label
items.description: what the option does (1-2 short sentences)
items.usage_tip: when or why to use it

manuals.title: Main Menu
manuals.summary: Central entry point of DayPass. Every menu uses the same keys: a number opens an option, 0 goes back (or exits here), q quits DayPass and h opens the manual of the screen.
manuals.reachable_from: Runs at the end of the installer / DayPass start

manuals.title: Package Profiles & Dependencies
manuals.summary: Installs the package profiles from config/package_profiles.json. Each profile shows its resolved package plan before anything is installed; failed required packages roll the profile back.

manuals.title: Hardware & USB Tethering Manager
manuals.summary: Shows USB devices (lsusb, or sysfs when usbutils is missing), USB network interfaces by kernel driver (rndis_host, cdc_ether, cdc_ncm, ipheth = phone tethering; qmi_wwan, cdc_mbim = modems), modem ports and WAN metrics.

manuals.title: Network & Routing Configuration
manuals.summary: Manages the home Wi-Fi access point, the isolated guest network, the router LAN IP, multi-WAN balancing, live speed monitoring and DNS mode.

manuals.title: Wi-Fi Access Point (Home WiFi)
manuals.summary: Manages only the Access Point interfaces of the home Wi-Fi on every radio; station/WWAN interfaces are never modified.

manuals.title: Guest Network & Bandwidth Control
manuals.summary: Builds an isolated guest LAN on 192.168.200.0/24 with its own DHCP server, firewall zone and optional guest Wi-Fi.

manuals.title: Guest Bandwidth Control (QoS)
manuals.summary: Caps guest speed with either lightweight tc rules or SQM using the Cake algorithm. Known issues: the tc directions are swapped (the download value limits upload and vice versa) and SQM targets the interface name guest instead of the bridge device.

manuals.title: DNS Manager
manuals.summary: Controls how the router resolves names for the local network. The status header shows the active mode, the active transport engine and the current dnsmasq upstreams. The chosen mode is remembered under /etc/daypass/dns/mode.

manuals.title: DNS Resolution Recovery
manuals.summary: Temporary DNS switch that is offered by the network checker when domain resolution fails. It changes DNS only for the current session and is not a replacement for the permanent DNS Manager.
manuals.reachable_from: Offered by the network checker when DNS resolution fails

manuals.title: Multi-WAN Load Balancer
manuals.summary: Adds USB tethering and a Wi-Fi hotspot as extra internet sources and writes an mwan3 setup over wan, wan_usb and wwan. Links are used in priority order: wan, then USB, then Wi-Fi.

manuals.title: Network Info & Speed Monitor
manuals.summary: Diagnostic panel that reports public IP details and can show live WAN bandwidth. The panel also reports offline state when no provider can be reached.

manuals.title: Proxy & Tunnel Engine Manager
manuals.summary: Transport engines and everything that acts on the active engine: nodes and subscriptions, traffic routing, routing profiles and Cloudflare Clean IP. Balancing and health checks are in Main menu -> 5.

manuals.title: Config Manager (Nodes & Subscriptions)
manuals.summary: Local node store for single share links and subscription links. Configs live in /etc/daypass/proxy/configs and the header shows the active transport engine.

manuals.title: Traffic Routing / Shunt Rules
manuals.summary: Applies a routing mode to the active transport engine. Passwall and Passwall2 get the mode through their own settings (Iran Direct builds a shunt node); sing-box and Xray get a DayPass TPROXY rule set; WireGuard and OpenVPN get a DayPass policy route into the tunnel.

manuals.title: Transport Engines
manuals.summary: Proxy & Tunnel Engine Manager. The list shows every engine DayPass supports (Passwall, Passwall2, sing-box, Xray, WireGuard, OpenVPN), whether it is installed and running, how it intercepts traffic (self, tproxy or tunnel) and which one is active. Pick a number to open the engine.

manuals.title: Node Load Balancing
manuals.summary: Probes the nodes of the active transport engine and switches to the best one for the chosen mode. Nodes are Passwall nodes, WireGuard peers, OpenVPN instances or sing-box/Xray outbounds.

manuals.title: Load Balancing Modes
manuals.summary: The mode list shown by Set Balancing Mode. Each Apply probes the selected nodes and uses the mode to pick the next active node.

manuals.title: Node Health Checker
manuals.summary: Tests whether saved nodes are reachable by probing the host and port inside each share link (TCP connect, or a UDP probe for kcp, quic, hysteria and tuic links) and reports approximate latency in milliseconds. Results are only displayed and are not used by the balancer.

manuals.title: Routing Profiles
manuals.summary: Ready-made traffic profiles that apply a routing mode to the active transport engine and remember the active profile. The header shows the active profile and the current routing mode.

manuals.title: Clean IP Manager (Cloudflare)
manuals.summary: Scans candidate Cloudflare IPs on a config's own port, then rewrites the address inside the share link when the config can really be fronted by Cloudflare: vless, vmess or trojan over ws, httpupgrade, h2, grpc, xhttp or splithttp. Reality, QUIC protocols (hysteria, hysteria2, tuic, naive+quic) and shadowsocks are refused and left untouched. The header shows the detected proxy core.

manuals.title: Clean IP Test Mode
manuals.summary: Test depth that Find Clean IP for a Config asks for before scanning the candidate IP list.

manuals.title: Node Balancer & Health Diagnostics
manuals.summary: Probes the nodes of the active transport engine and switches between them. The status block shows the balancing mode, selected nodes, engine and current node.

manuals.title: System Maintenance & Backup
manuals.summary: Maintenance tools, DayPass engine config backups, logs and package updates.

manuals.title: Maintenance & Recovery
manuals.summary: Repair and clean-up tools for the system module. The same module also powers the read-only Hardware & Resource Status screen (main menu option 5), which shows architecture, OpenWrt release, RAM and storage usage.

manuals.title: Service Manager
manuals.summary: Service helpers for the core network stack: enable, start, stop and status checks used by other modules. post_install_services_init bundles them for a post-deployment pass and has no interactive menu, so the entries below describe the services it controls rather than menu numbers.

reference_manual.description: Full reference: navigation tree, articles, terminology, known issues and the L1-L7 network layer map. Not rendered by the in-app viewer; read it with jq.
